solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rhode Island group's award

parts.note: RI is the US state abbreviation for Rhode Island
a band is a group, e.g. of musicians

explanation.surface: A band from Rhode Island picks up a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A riband is a ribbon given as a prize or decoration, such as the Blue Riband trophy.

clue.text: Informer, one on fixed allowance

parts.note: a rat is an informer, a grass
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A police informant is living on a set payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A ration is a fixed portion of food or goods allotted to each person.

clue.text: Newly feed a stubborn animal used for work

indicators.note: newly signals the fodder's letters freshly arranged into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Instructions to feed a stubborn working animal again.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast of burden is an animal such as a donkey or ox kept to carry loads and do labour.

clue.text: Opening section of piano's trill

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The opening passage of a piano piece includes a trill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks musical, like the start of a piece, but it means an orifice.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostril is one of the two external openings of the nose.

clue.text: Monotony of new diet, uniform beginning and end

indicators.note: a new version of the word diet has its letters rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: beginning and end asks for only the first and last letters of uniform

parts.note: the word whose outer letters are taken

explanation.surface: Eating the same new diet in the same uniform every day is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns DIET into TEDI; 'beginning and end' of uniform gives U and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium is boring sameness, which is exactly what monotony describes.

clue.text: Seems a girl regularly used communication system

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

parts.note: the words whose alternate letters are taken

explanation.surface: A girl apparently relied on one way of keeping in touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Email is electronic mail, a system for sending messages between computers.

clue.text: "He's no team player!" Aunt is livid I'd fouled up

indicators.note: fouled up means messed up, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A furious aunt complains about someone who spoiled things by playing for himself.
explanation.definitionFit: An individualist acts independently and goes his own way rather than cooperating in a group.

clue.text: Due for payment, mother? True, unfortunately

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of true are mixed up

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Mother admits a bill must be paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond or policy that matures reaches the date when its payment falls due.

clue.text: Route's distinctive quality entertaining Poles

indicators.note: entertaining guests means holding them within, so the poles go inside

parts.note: a trait is a distinguishing characteristic
N and S, the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A road's special character is that it hosts visitors from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland but means the compass points N and S, which go inside TRAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A transit is a passage or way across, as in a transit route through a country.

clue.text: Toper's second return, always half-ignored and not to be mentioned

indicators.note: ignored means those letters are left out of the drinker

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker, taken here as written
always is E'ER, the poetic contraction; half of it is ER
RET is an abbreviation for return

explanation.surface: A drunkard's later homecoming, half forgotten as ever, is best kept quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: E'ER is a poetic contraction of ever, which is always; half of it, ER, is ignored in TOPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something top secret is classified at the highest level and must not be talked about.

clue.text: Inspection as unusual deficit is tackled at first

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of each of the five words before it

parts.note: first letter A
first letter U
first letter D
first letter I
first letter T

explanation.surface: An unexpected shortfall is dealt with by first checking the books.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official examination of accounts, a formal check or inspection.

clue.text: Notebook Jack's lost depicting furry swimmer

indicators.note: Jack being lost means the letter for jack is dropped

parts.note: a jotter is a small notebook
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A sketchbook with animal drawings has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: A jotter is a British word for a small notebook for jotting things down.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a sleek-furred mammal that spends much of its life swimming in rivers.

clue.text: Idle chatter from friend, a part of speech cut short

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the word is lopped off

parts.note: a verb is one of the parts of speech

explanation.surface: A friend's gossip is interrupted mid-sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaver is lengthy, pointless talk or fuss, a near-synonym of idle chatter.

clue.text: Home Counties criminal seen by Cornwall river? That's not true

indicators.note: seen by places the river beside the other pieces, which follow it

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
SE, the south-east of England, where the Home Counties around London lie
a hood is a gangster, a criminal

explanation.surface: A crook from near London spotted beside a Cornish river? A lie.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in England's south-east, hence SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsehood is a lie, a statement that is untrue, which the definition describes as a thing.

clue.text: Old Boy's remedy far from clear

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for Old Boy, a former pupil, with the S of the possessive
a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: A former pupil's treatment remains a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: An Old Boy is a British term for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure means vague or hard to understand, the opposite of clear.

clue.text: A world of energy in factory?

indicators.note: in puts the energy letter inside the factory

parts.note: a plant is a factory
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Asks whether a factory makes a world of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet is a world, a large body orbiting a star.

clue.text: Media boss offering some carrot I decide after reflection

indicators.note: after reflection means the letters are seen as in a mirror, backwards
some means only part of the words is used, a stretch inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the words carrot, I and decide

explanation.surface: A newspaper chief offers vegetables and makes a decision after thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after reflection' sounds like careful thought but means reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is in charge of a newspaper, magazine or broadcast, so a boss in the media.

clue.text: Wash three articles from abroad

parts.note: two of the three articles: French la (the) and un (a)
the third foreign article, German der (the); 'from abroad' marks all three as foreign words

explanation.surface: Instructions to clean three imported items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' looks like goods, but means grammatical articles: French la and un, German der.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder clothes is to wash and iron them.

clue.text: Live comfortably supporting daughter

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits under the daughter

parts.note: to live well is to live comfortably

explanation.surface: Someone lives in comfort while helping out a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to reside or live somewhere.

clue.text: Turf lotteries recalled

indicators.note: recalled, called back, has the word read backwards

parts.note: draws are lotteries, prize draws

explanation.surface: A gambling scheme on the racecourse turf is withdrawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A sward is an expanse of short grass, i.e. turf.

clue.text: For example, demand for payment on return? Gentle reminder

indicators.note: on return has the pieces read in the backward direction

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example
a dun is a demand for payment of a debt

explanation.surface: A bill sent back with a polite prompt to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Dun, as a noun or verb, is an old word for pressing a debtor.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a light push, figuratively a gentle prompt or reminder.

clue.text: Time with our first journeyman?

parts.note: 1ST written with the 1 as the letter I

explanation.surface: Asks whether time spent with our leading craftsman makes him a traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: A journeyman is a qualified tradesman, but the question mark lets it read literally as a man on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is someone travelling for pleasure, a man who makes journeys.

clue.text: Complicated situation — ultimately reluctant to reach point of view

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of reluctant

parts.note: last letter T
an angle is a viewpoint or slant

explanation.surface: A hesitant person finally forming an opinion gets into a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangle is a confused mess, a muddled or complicated situation.

clue.text: One advising blokes to rest initially

parts.note: blokes are men

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of rest

parts.note: first letter R

explanation.surface: An adviser tells the men to take a break.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloke is everyday British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A mentor is a trusted counsellor who guides and advises a less experienced person.
